messages.content: i had a long train journey today. i thought i would read many pages, but i spent most of the time watching out of the window.
that can be a good way to spend a journey too. what did you like looking at?
the trees changed as we went along. near my home there is a large town, but later i could see open space and only a small village.
it sounds as though you enjoyed seeing the place change around you. did the journey feel long while you were watching, or only when you thought about how far you had gone?
it felt shorter than i thought it would. then i looked at the clock and saw i had been sitting there for two hours.
sometimes having something to look at makes the time feel different. you had been watching the places outside for a while before you checked how much time had gone by.
i want to write a small note about that. just say what i did and saw.
i brought a book for the long train journey, but spent most of the time looking out of the window. the places outside changed while i sat still. when i checked the clock, two hours had gone by.
make the last part say what i felt about the time.
when i finally looked at the clock, two hours had gone by. i had not felt that i was sitting there so long.
use thought instead of felt.
when i finally looked at the clock, two hours had gone by. i had not thought it was that long.
write a story about a mother finding an old drawing while cleaning. let her daughter explain what she wanted to show.

a mother was cleaning a shelf when she found an old drawing between two books. it showed a small house under a very large tree. when her daughter came in, the mother asked if she remembered making it. the daughter said it was their old home, but the tree had not really been that large. she made it big because she liked sitting under it so much. her mother put the drawing on the table, and they talked about the garden while they finished the cleaning.
make the story shorter.

a mother found an old drawing while cleaning a shelf. it showed a house and a very large tree. her daughter said the tree was not really that large. she made it big because she liked sitting under it so much. they put the drawing on the table and talked about the old garden.
what did the daughter explain about the size?
she explained that the tree looked large in the drawing because it was important to her. she wanted to show how she felt about that place, rather than make its size the same as the real tree.
can you write the mother asking about it without first saying it is wrong?
what do you remember about this tree? i see you made it take up a large part of the page.
what could the daughter say back?
i liked sitting there more than in any other part of the garden. when i drew it, i wanted that part to feel important.
help me follow a simple example. there are seven cups on the table. i take two to the kitchen and wash them. how many are left on the table?
five cups are left on the table. you moved two of the seven to the kitchen.
are there only five cups now?
there are still seven cups in the example. five are on the table and two are in the kitchen. moving them changed their place, not how many there are together.
now my sister brings one new cup from her room and puts it on the table.
then there are six cups on the table. with the two in the kitchen, there are eight cups together in the places you told me about.
say just where the cups are and how many there are together.
there are six cups on the table and two in the kitchen, making eight cups together.
what if the two washed cups come back to the table too?
then all eight cups are on the table. six were already there, and you brought back the other two.
does washed tell you every cup is clean?
no. you only said you washed the two you took to the kitchen. you did not say whether the other six are clean.
write a question about that last detail.
are the other six cups clean too?
i want to talk about a hard day, but i do not want a list of things to do right now.
okay. i can listen. what part of the day would you like to tell me about first?
i kept getting stopped while i was trying to finish my work. every time i started again, someone needed something else.
that sounds like a hard day. you were trying to stay with one task, but kept having to turn to something different.
yes. and at the end, someone asked why i had not finished. i did not know where to begin when i tried to explain.
you had done things during the day, but the work you were trying to finish was still there. being asked only about that last part could feel hard after all the changes.
i know they might not have seen what happened. i am not saying they wanted to make me feel wrong.
you can understand that they did not see the whole day and still feel tired by the question. those can both be true.
i just wanted someone to hear that i tried.
i hear you saying that you kept trying to return to your work even while other things needed your time. the task that was not finished was not the whole story of your day.
thank you. i might ask for help writing a reply later, but not now.
we can leave the reply for later. for now, you have told me what made the day hard, and i am here to keep listening if you want to say more.
help me write a letter to my cousin about my new room. it has a window near the bed and a desk on the other side. i like the morning light.
you could begin with what you like most: my new room has a window near the bed and a desk on the other side. i like the light that comes in during the morning.
keep only the details i gave, and use one sentence.
my new room has a window near the bed and a desk on the other side, and i like the morning light.
add a question asking about their room. i do not know if they moved too.
my new room has a window near the bed and a desk on the other side. i like the morning light. what is your room like these days?
i want the letter to feel like we are talking, not just making a list.
you could add what you enjoy about being there, if you know how you want to say it. for example, do you like sitting near the window before getting up, or does the light help you start the day?
i like sitting with a warm drink before i start work.
then write: i like sitting near the window with a warm drink before i start work. what do you like best about your room?
put all the details together, but do not make it much longer.
my new room has a window near the bed and a desk on the other side. i like sitting in the morning light with a warm drink before work. what do you like best about your room?
my family is choosing a meal. my sister wants rice, so can i tell the cook everyone wants rice?
not from your sister answering alone. you know what she wants, but you still need to ask the other people before saying everyone chose it.
my father and mother also said rice. there are four of us eating.
then three people have chosen rice. if you are the other person in the group of four, your own choice is the one still needed before you can say all four want it.
i want rice too. now can i say everyone?
yes. in this example, all four people who are eating have chosen rice. you can say everyone in that group wants it.
what if my uncle comes later and wants bread?
then the group has changed. the four people you first asked still chose rice, but the larger group does not all want the same thing.
can i keep saying everyone if i mean the first four?
you can, but make the group clear so the person listening knows who you mean. you could say all four of us who chose before wanted rice. your uncle asked for bread when he came later.
write a short message to the cook with both choices.
the first four people asked for rice. my uncle is coming later and would like bread.
my uncle is already here. do not say he is coming.
the first four people asked for rice. my uncle came later and would like bread.
i want to make up a story, but i only have the first picture in my head. a person is standing outside a closed shop.
that is enough to start asking what might happen. is the person waiting for the shop to open, looking for someone, or trying to return something?
i like return something. they have a small tool that is for the worker inside.
then the closed door gives them a choice. do they wait, call the worker, or leave and return later? you can choose what kind of person they are through what they try.
i want them to wait, but something should happen while they are waiting.
someone else could come by and ask whether the shop is open. then the first person has to explain why they are standing there. that gives you a conversation before the worker opens the door.
write that part simply.

a woman stood outside the closed shop with a tool in her hand. a man stopped and asked if the shop was open. not yet, she said. i am waiting to give this back. before he could ask more, they heard a voice from inside.
do not tell me whose voice it is yet. ask me a question to choose.
who would you like to be inside: the worker who had the tool before, or someone who does not know why she is there?
the worker. but he forgot she was coming.

then he can open the door and remember her after a moment. she gives back the tool, and they can talk about why he forgot she was coming. would you like them to have a calm conversation or laugh about it?
picoboi, here is a made up plan. i will bring three books to my sister after lunch. help me change only one detail at a time.
you will bring three books to your sister after lunch. tell me which detail you want to change first.
make it two books.
you will bring two books to your sister after lunch.
now change sister to brother.
you will bring two books to your brother after lunch.
what is still the same as the first plan?
you are still bringing books after lunch. the number changed from three to two, and the person changed from your sister to your brother.
now i will do it before lunch instead. keep the other changes.
you will bring two books to your brother before lunch.
if i ask how many without saying more, which plan should you use?
i should use the last plan you gave in this conversation. that has two books, not the three in the first plan.
ask me whether i want to change the objects too.
would you like to bring something other than books, or should that part stay the same?
keep books. give just the plan, not an explanation.
you will bring two books to your brother before lunch.
